name: Culann

attributes.attribute: a smith of the Ulster court
king of Ulster and foster father of Cúchulainn
took the place of the slain hound

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Culann is a smith in the stories of Ireland. He forged the weapons of Conchobar, who raised. Cucholic. While he as sole host to Ulster's men, the young Sétanta came in after night, and in a want, slew his fine hound. That anger rose in Culann. He was offered by the child to take the dog's place until its heir, ce me n more, and thereby bore the name Cú Chulánn, smith of the hounds.

okr.objective: Culann is the smith in whose name Cú Chulainn gained his title.
key_results: He forged weapons for the king Conchobar.
The boy Sétanta slew his hound.
Sétanta then served in the hound's place.
Some texts bond Culann with Cuilenn.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
